## Solution

We assume $[L:K]<\infty$ (otherwise $\det_K$ of a $K$-linear endomorphism of the infinite-dimensional space $L^{n\times n}$ is not defined); write $d=[L:K]$.

**Key decomposition.** Define the left- and right-multiplication maps
$$L_A(B)=AB,\qquad R_{A^{-1}}(B)=BA^{-1}.$$
Both are $K$-linear endomorphisms of $M_n(L)=L^{n\times n}$, they commute (left vs. right multiplication), and
$$C_A = R_{A^{-1}}\circ L_A = L_A\circ R_{A^{-1}}.$$
Hence
$$\det_K(C_A)=\det_K(L_A)\cdot\det_K(R_{A^{-1}}). \tag{1}$$

**Determinant of an $L$-linear map viewed as $K$-linear.** Let $T:L^m\to L^m$ be $L$-linear with matrix $M\in M_m(L)$. We claim
$$\det_K(T)=N_{L/K}\!\bigl(\det_L M\bigr), \tag{2}$$
where $N_{L/K}$ is the field norm. Indeed, $L^m$ as a $K$-space is $\bigoplus_{i=1}^m L$; for a diagonal $M=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_m)$, $T$ acts on the $i$-th summand by $x\mapsto \alpha_i x$, whose $K$-determinant is $N_{L/K}(\alpha_i)$, giving $\det_K(T)=\prod_i N_{L/K}(\alpha_i)=N_{L/K}(\prod_i\alpha_i)=N_{L/K}(\det_L M)$. The general case follows by Gaussian elimination over $L$ (row swaps contribute signs whose norm is $\pm1$, and transvections have $L$-determinant $1$, hence $K$-determinant $1$), using multiplicativity of $N_{L/K}$.

**Computing $\det_K(L_A)$.** View $M_n(L)$ as an $L$-vector space (dimension $n^2$) by splitting into columns: $M_n(L)\cong (L^n)^{\oplus n}$. The map $L_A$ acts columnwise by $v\mapsto Av$, an $L$-linear map of $L^n$ with $L$-determinant $\det_L A$. Therefore
$$\det_L(L_A)=(\det_L A)^n,$$
and by (2),
$$\det_K(L_A)=N_{L/K}\!\bigl((\det_L A)^n\bigr)=N_{L/K}(\det_L A)^n. \tag{3}$$

**Computing $\det_K(R_{A^{-1}})$.** Split $M_n(L)$ into rows: $M_n(L)\cong (L^n)^{\oplus n}$ (row vectors). The map $R_{A^{-1}}$ acts rowwise by $w\mapsto wA^{-1}$, an $L$-linear map with $L$-determinant $\det_L(A^{-1})=(\det_L A)^{-1}$. Thus
$$\det_L(R_{A^{-1}})=(\det_L A)^{-n},$$
and by (2),
$$\det_K(R_{A^{-1}})=N_{L/K}\!\bigl((\det_L A)^{-n}\bigr)=N_{L/K}(\det_L A)^{-n}. \tag{4}$$

**Combining.** Substituting (3) and (4) into (1),
$$\det_K(C_A)=N_{L/K}(\det_L A)^n\cdot N_{L/K}(\det_L A)^{-n}=1.$$

**Verification on the hint case.** Take $n=2$, $K=\mathbb{R}$, $L=\mathbb{C}$, $A=\operatorname{diag}(i,1)$. Then $N_{\mathbb{C}/\mathbb{R}}(\det_{\mathbb C}A)=N_{\mathbb{C}/\mathbb{R}}(i)=i\bar i=1$, and the formula gives $\det_{\mathbb R}(C_A)=1$. Directly: with $\mathbb R$-basis $\{E_{jk},\,iE_{jk}\}_{j,k=1,2}$ of $M_2(\mathbb C)$, one checks $C_A$ fixes $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{E_{11},iE_{11},E_{22},iE_{22}\}$ pointwise, acts on $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{E_{12},iE_{12}\}$ by $E_{12}\mapsto iE_{12}\mapsto -E_{12}$ (matrix $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$, det $1$), and on $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{E_{21},iE_{21}\}$ by $E_{21}\mapsto -iE_{21}\mapsto E_{21}$ (matrix $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$, det $1$). Total determinant $=1\cdot1\cdot1\cdot1=1$, confirming the formula.

---

**Answer.** For any finite extension $K\subset L$ and any $A\in GL(n,L)$,
$$\boxed{\det_K(C_A)=1}.$$
The determinant is independent of both $n$ and $A$; it is always $1$.
